newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists would do better than Juppe - poll.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists would do better than Juppe - poll.

text.p: French voters believe the opposition Socialist party, routed at the last elections, would do a better job than Prime Minister Alain Juppe's centre-right coalition, an opinion poll showed on Monday.

The BVA survey for the daily Liberation indicated that most French people reckoned draft Socialist policies, such as cuts in value added tax, creating 350,000 jobs for the young or cutting the working week to 35 hours from 39, were feasible.
Socialist party leaders outlined the policies this month ahead of the next legislative elections in 1998.

Forty percent of 953 people interviewed on November 15 and 16 felt the Socialist party would do better than the government in grappling with record unemployment and sluggish economic growth if it were in power today.
Twenty-four percent believed the Socialists would do worse, 30 percent thought it would neither do better nor worse and the remaining six percent had no opinion.
Juppe took over last year, three years after a landslide ousted a Socialist-led government, blamed for rising unemployment and creeping corruption in politics.
